headline: Sales grow on Greif deal, but profit slips as costs bite
summary_short: Packaging Corporation of America reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $2,489.9M, up 14.7% y/y and 5.2% q/q on the Greif acquisition and record legacy corrugated shipments, while diluted EPS fell 19.5% y/y to $2.15 as special items and higher freight/corporate costs offset the acquired volumes.
summary_long: Net income fell to $192.1M ($2.15 diluted EPS, -19.5% y/y) despite sales up 14.7% y/y to $2,489.9M, as the newly acquired Greif operations added $0.14/share while the legacy business lost $0.27/share to higher freight ($0.26), corporate costs ($0.12), unfavorable packaging price/mix ($0.11) and integration/restructuring charges, partly offset by record legacy corrugated volumes (+4.1%/day) and lower maintenance outages. Excluding special items, EPS was $2.35, $0.02 above the company's own Q2 guidance of $2.33. Long-term debt rose to $3,968.9M (+60.4% y/y) on Greif-related financing; cash fell to $442.8M from $787.9M a year ago. Management guides Q3 2026 EPS of $2.91 excluding special items, its first Q3 outlook of the cycle.

drivers.explanation: CEO Mark Kowlzan cites an all-time quarterly record in legacy corrugated shipments, the first realized price increase taking hold, and the acquired Greif business contributing via strong plant volumes and improved mill performance.
Total corrugated products shipments rose 24.3% y/y including the Greif acquisition; legacy packaging shipments were up 4.1% per day y/y with the same number of shipping days.
GAAP EPS fell $0.52 y/y on a $0.39 swing to net special items (mill restructuring, facility closures, acquisition costs) plus $0.13 lower earnings excluding those items.

Excluding special items, the legacy business lost $0.27/share to higher freight ($0.26), corporate costs ($0.12) and unfavorable packaging price/mix ($0.11), partly offset by legacy volume gains; the acquired Greif business added $0.14/share, including a $0.04 depreciation benefit from purchase-accounting adjustments.

Segment operating income fell to $291.2M from $333.7M as Corporate and Other costs widened to -$56.3M from -$38.4M and Packaging segment income absorbed $8.3M of facility-closure and $6.3M of Wallula mill restructuring charges.
Debt rose to $3,968.9M from $2,475.2M as the release attributes higher interest expense partly to indebtedness incurred for the Greif acquisition.
